playerText.title: Dead Letters
playerText.summary: Trace the counterfeit signal into the Hecate Drift, establish what is operating near Hecate Seven, and leave the site in a defensible state.
The preserved traffic points toward Hecate Seven, where hazardous conditions make approach, investigation, and withdrawal consequential.

The installation is an old Dominion-origin message relay containing intercepted and fabricated personal traffic; it is both physical evidence and a collection of lives exposed without consent, even before individual messages are authenticated.
The relay is one node in a distributed system built to predict community responses and store possible future scenarios, but this node alone cannot identify the network's controller.

The evidence supports local postwar access and a current Starfleet Intelligence handshake; a Demeris traffic-maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn provides the next defensible lead without proving who controls the wider operation.
Voiceprints, private turns of phrase, and transmission scars establish that the relay's counterfeit messages were assembled from authentic personal traffic rather than invented wholesale.
Maintenance traces establish repeated local postwar access and a recent Starfleet Intelligence handshake, without identifying the wider operation's controller.
A Demeris traffic-maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn is the next corroborated route of inquiry, not proof that Solenn controls the network.
Captain Nella Ivers permits the messages involving her crew to be used as bounded operational evidence, but refuses broad publication of the private originals.
Director Nia Kessler will support analysis only if an independent custodian can audit who accesses the archive and challenge Starfleet's use of it.
Administrator Asha Prel asks that relief recipients named in the stolen traffic be shielded from publication and offers Cardassian convoy records as a privacy-preserving corroboration route.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes the actual result of the approach or operating-position attempt at Hecate Seven.

values.guidance: The crew establishes a defensible operating position without a material access cost.
The crew establishes access while taking a material, recorded cost or limitation.
Conditions or opposition prevent the crew from maintaining access despite a genuine attempt.

exclusions: An order to approach, a course setting, arrival nearby, or a proposed plan does not establish the result of access.

interpretation.guidance: Record only an explicit player decision to withdraw or decline the hazardous approach while preserving a responsible handoff or alternate-investigation route.

values.guidance: The player explicitly chooses a responsible withdrawal instead of attempting or continuing direct access.

exclusions: Caution, delay, requesting more information, or discussing withdrawal is not an explicit decision to withdraw.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration depicts actual sensor, physical, or technical contact sufficient to characterize the Hecate installation.
exclusions: Planning contact, ordering a scan, approaching the site, or receiving an unverified distant indication is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose the aggregate finding that the installation is an old Dominion-origin relay containing intercepted and fabricated personal traffic, and that the human archive has independent ethical stakes. Leave individual message authenticity to its separate evidence route.
exclusions: A generic relay sighting, one recovered message, a speculative Dominion reference, or an unexplained archive does not disclose the aggregate finding; do not treat discovery of the archive as authentication of every message.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration depicts enough recovered or analyzed system evidence to support an architectural assessment.
exclusions: Beginning analysis, copying an unidentified fragment, guessing at a network, or issuing an analysis order is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose the bounded architectural conclusion: this is a distributed predictive node holding future scenarios, while this node alone does not identify the wider controller.
exclusions: Do not turn architectural evidence into attribution to Pale Lantern, Farwatch, Holt, Rourke, or any other controller not proven here.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration depicts recovered logs, traffic records, handshakes, or equivalent direct evidence sufficient to establish access history and a next lead.
exclusions: A search order, an incomplete download, a hunch about local access, or an unexplained account name is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration depicts credible corroboration through Prel or Cardassian records, Compact testimony, traffic residue, or another established source after direct evidence is unavailable.
exclusions: Invented convenient evidence, an unsupported inference, or merely naming a possible source does not establish alternate corroboration.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose only the supported access history and lead: local postwar access, a current Starfleet Intelligence handshake, and the Demeris account associated with Mira Solenn, without claiming the wider controller is proven.
exclusions: Do not attribute the operation to Pale Lantern, Farwatch, Holt, Rourke, or Wayward Sun from this evidence alone.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only after Captain Nella Ivers has personally reviewed an identified sample involving her convoy and stated what use she will permit.
exclusions: Merely recognizing Ivers's name, leaving her a message, or assuming prior cooperation implies consent is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose Ivers's exact boundary: operational use is permitted, but broad publication of the private originals is not.
exclusions: Do not treat consent to operational analysis as consent to public release or permanent unrestricted retention.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only after Director Nia Kessler has reviewed enough identified material to respond as a representative of affected Compact communities.
exclusions: A generic briefing to the Compact or an unanswered consultation request is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose Kessler's demand for independently auditable custody with authority to challenge Starfleet access.
exclusions: Do not reduce her position to anti-Starfleet suspicion or imply she demands public release.

interpretation.guidance: Claim after Administrator Asha Prel is consulted about named relief recipients or, when the archive is unavailable, about matching the known counterfeit traffic against protected Cardassian convoy records.
exclusions: Invoking Cardassian records without Prel's participation or safeguards is not this consultation.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose both parts of Prel's position: protect named relief recipients and use guarded convoy records as an alternate corroboration route.
exclusions: Do not imply the protected records may be broadly copied or that Prel can consent for every person named in the archive.

interpretation.guidance: Claim when technical comparison and an affected person's recognition together establish that counterfeit messages contain authentic private source material.
exclusions: Technical resemblance alone, an emotional reaction alone, or a generic claim that the messages feel real is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose that authentic private communications were recombined into false messages, identifying the evidentiary and consent stakes without exposing unnecessary contents.
exclusions: Do not narrate private message details that have not been deliberately disclosed in play.

interpretation.guidance: Claim when maintenance traces independently establish local postwar use and a recent Starfleet Intelligence handshake.
exclusions: The relay's Dominion construction, a current power signature, or a speculative Starfleet link is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose the bounded access history without folding it into attribution or the separate Demeris route.
exclusions: Do not identify an operator or claim the intelligence handshake proves authorization.

interpretation.guidance: Claim when direct relay records connect the access history to a Demeris maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn.
exclusions: A Demeris name without routing continuity or a Solenn association without the account trail is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Claim when Ivers's retained traffic or Prel's protected convoy records independently reconstruct the Demeris route after direct relay evidence is unavailable.
exclusions: A guessed destination, an unverified recollection, or evidence invented to replace the lost relay is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Disclose the Demeris account and Mira Solenn association as a corroborated next route, explicitly separating it from proof of control.
exclusions: Do not identify Solenn, Farwatch, Pale Lantern, Holt, Rourke, or Starfleet Intelligence as the network controller.

interpretation.guidance: Record only the player's explicit informed choice for the physical relay after its character and human stakes are known.

values.guidance: Preserve the relay under accountable isolation.
Permit bounded observation or tracing with containment safeguards.
Destroy the relay only after preserving a deliberate evidence copy.
Destroy the relay without preserving a system-evidence copy.

exclusions: A crew recommendation, a hypothetical option, a provisional discussion, or an action before the player knows the relay's character is not the player's informed decision.

interpretation.guidance: Record only the player's explicit decision to leave the inaccessible relay in place as part of a responsible withdrawal.

values.guidance: The player explicitly leaves the relay in place and transfers the unresolved risk into a recorded handoff.

exclusions: Being delayed, forced away, or merely discussing withdrawal does not establish the player's decision to leave the relay in place.

interpretation.guidance: Record only the player's explicit informed custody and release policy for the recovered human archive.

values.guidance: Protect the archive under accountable joint custody with affected communities or trusted local partners.
Protect the archive under tightly restricted custody and access.
Authorize broad release or restitution despite the privacy exposure it creates.
Transfer primary custody to Starfleet Intelligence with the resulting opacity recorded.

exclusions: A crew suggestion, discussing principles, beginning recovery, or assuming Starfleet owns the material is not the player's explicit policy decision.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that the relay is actually preserved and isolated under accountable control.

values.guidance: The relay is preserved, unable to transmit or reactivate freely, and held under accountable isolation.

exclusions: Ordering isolation, beginning containment, or assuming a successful lockout does not establish the result.

interpretation.guidance: Claim the actual aggregate result of bounded observation only after its containment and exposure consequences are depicted.

values.guidance: Observation produces usable value while containment holds and exposure remains bounded.
Observation materially exposes the Breckenridge, the site, or another protected party to the network.

exclusions: Starting a tracer, setting safeguards, or observing one response does not establish the final containment result.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes both a preserved evidence copy and actual destruction of the physical relay.

values.guidance: A deliberate evidence copy survives and the physical relay is destroyed.

exclusions: Preparing charges, beginning a copy, ordering destruction, or destroying the relay without a usable copy does not establish this result.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes actual destruction without a usable system-evidence copy.

values.guidance: The physical relay is destroyed and no usable system-evidence copy survives.

exclusions: An order, an attempted destruction, or uncertainty about whether a copy survived is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that the relay has been lost, seized, removed, or placed beyond accountable control.

values.guidance: The relay is no longer under accountable control because it was lost or seized.

exclusions: A threat, attempted seizure, temporary interruption, or fear of losing the relay is not an actual loss.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that the crew leaves the relay in place because of responsible withdrawal or forced loss of access.

values.guidance: The relay remains at the site outside the Breckenridge's direct custody, with the unresolved risk recorded.

exclusions: A pause, temporary retreat, or uncertain access does not establish that the relay has been left in place as the mission disposition.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes actual accountable joint custody and protection for the recovered archive.

values.guidance: The archive is protected under credible joint custody with affected communities or trusted local partners.

exclusions: Proposing joint custody, opening negotiations, or transferring an unverified copy is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes actual restricted custody with enforceable access limits.

values.guidance: The archive is protected under tightly restricted, accountable access.

exclusions: Declaring material classified, requesting secure storage, or planning access rules is insufficient.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that the archive or its messages are actually released broadly enough to create material privacy consequences.

values.guidance: The archive receives broad release or restitution, preserving access while accepting significant privacy exposure.

exclusions: Discussing release, notifying one family, or preparing a review copy does not establish broad release.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that Starfleet Intelligence actually assumes primary custody, with local accountability limits recorded.

values.guidance: Starfleet Intelligence takes primary custody and the resulting loss of transparency is recorded.

exclusions: An Intelligence request, a handshake, classification language, or an intended transfer does not establish custody.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that the human archive or its meaningful contents escape accountable custody.

values.guidance: The archive is seized, exposed, copied beyond control, or otherwise lost from accountable custody.

exclusions: A threatened breach, uncertain copying, or a temporary custody dispute is not an established loss of control.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted narration establishes that no usable human archive is recovered into the Breckenridge's accountable custody.

values.guidance: The archive is not recovered because it was destroyed, left inaccessible, or remained at the site.

exclusions: An incomplete search, delayed recovery, or uncertainty about surviving material is not a final not-recovered result.

playerText.summary: The installation is a Dominion-origin message relay containing intercepted and fabricated personal traffic, making its human archive a separate custody problem even before individual messages are authenticated.
The relay is one distributed predictive node holding possible future scenarios; the evidence does not by itself identify the wider controller.
The supported access history points to local postwar use, a current Starfleet Intelligence handshake, and a Demeris maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn as the next lead.
Captain Ivers permits bounded operational use of her crew's messages, but not broad publication of the private originals.
Director Kessler requires independently auditable custody with standing to challenge Starfleet access.
Administrator Prel asks that named relief recipients be protected and offers guarded convoy records as an alternate route.
Technical comparison and personal recognition confirm that authentic private traffic was recombined into false messages.
Maintenance traces establish local postwar use and a recent Starfleet Intelligence handshake without proving who operated the wider network.
Direct records or protected corroboration trace the next lead to a Demeris maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn, without proving control.

playerText.title: Establish a defensible position at Hecate Seven
playerText.summary: Find a safe way to investigate the site, accept a recorded access cost, or make a responsible withdrawal that preserves another route forward.

terminal.text: The Breckenridge established a defensible operating position at Hecate Seven.
The Hecate approach concluded with a material access cost or forced loss of position recorded.
The direct approach was responsibly declined and its unresolved risk was handed forward.

playerText.title: Establish what the Hecate Seven evidence proves
playerText.summary: Build the strongest supportable account from what can be recovered at the site; missing direct evidence changes confidence and cost rather than blocking the campaign.

terminal.text: Direct evidence established the system's character, architecture, access history, and next lead.
Alternate corroboration preserved the next lead, but important direct evidence remained unavailable.

playerText.title: Resolve the site's custody
playerText.summary: Make informed choices about any dangerous or sensitive material you find, then establish what actually happens to it.

terminal.text: The physical system and human material reached an accountable protected disposition.
Custody was resolved with a deliberate operational, evidentiary, privacy, or transparency cost.
The unresolved site and material were left in place under a recorded forward handoff.
The system or human material escaped accountable control after the relevant risks were known.

playerText.title: The investigation continues after a loss of control
playerText.summary: The next lead survived, but forced access failure, exposure, or lost custody remains an active campaign consequence.

playerText.title: A responsible withdrawal preserves the investigation
playerText.summary: The Breckenridge avoided an unjustified hazard and preserved a corroborated route forward, while the unresolved Hecate site remains on the record.

playerText.title: Immediate privacy was protected at an evidentiary cost
playerText.summary: The dangerous system and unrecovered personal material were denied further use, while the loss of direct evidence limits what can be proven.

playerText.title: The truth moves forward with a recorded cost
playerText.summary: Usable evidence and the next lead survived, while access, destruction, privacy, or opaque custody costs remain part of the mission result.

playerText.title: Bounded observation remained contained
playerText.summary: The crew learned from the live system without losing containment, and the human material received an accountable disposition.

playerText.title: The site is preserved under accountable isolation
playerText.summary: The physical evidence is contained, the human material is protected, and the supported next lead can be pursued without overstating attribution.

target.playerSafeSetup: The strongest surviving evidence points to a Demeris traffic-maintenance account associated with Mira Solenn, giving the Breckenridge a defensible next lead.

mustNarrate: State the actual access, evidence, physical-system, and human-material results without upgrading partial success into total success.
Use only facts the player learned; if direct evidence was lost, describe the Demeris lead as corroborated rather than complete.
Carry forward exposure, lost custody, destruction, opaque custody, or responsible withdrawal as real consequences when recorded.
Frame Mira Solenn and the Demeris account as the next investigative lead, not as proof of who controls the wider operation.
mustNotReveal: Do not reveal Pale Lantern, Farwatch, Holt's wider role, Rourke's role, or the Wayward Sun compromise.
Do not claim the player discovered relay character or network architecture when those facts remain unknown.
Do not erase privacy, custody, access, evidence, or exposure costs.
Do not imply that destroying, preserving, observing, releasing, restricting, or handing off material was the player's choice unless the corresponding decision is recorded.
